1) Mucous membrane pemphigoid (cicatricial pemphigoid)
   - Supports: elderly patient with prominent palatal/oral erosions, subepidermal blister on H&E, linear IgG along the basement membrane on DIF.

2) Bullous pemphigoid
   - Supports: tense bullae on trunk/extremities, subepidermal bulla with eosinophils/neutrophils, linear BMZ IgG and good previous response to immunosuppression.

3) Paraneoplastic pemphigus (PNP)
   - Supports: combined pattern of BMZ linear staining and weak suprabasal/ intercellular IgG on DIF and atypical indirect IF (binding both roof and floor) — consider evaluation for occult neoplasia.

4) Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA)
   - Supports: subepidermal blister with neutrophil-rich infiltrate and indirect IF that can show dermal-side (floor) binding — dual binding might reflect mixed antibodies or technical variability.

5) Mixed/overlap autoimmune blistering disease (coexisting pemphigus + pemphigoid antibodies)
   - Supports: presence of both suprabasal weblike intercellular IgG and linear BMZ IgG, plus salt-split binding to both roof and floor consistent with multiple autoantibody specificities.

Recommendation: correlate these findings with targeted serologic testing (ELISA for BP180/BP230, desmoglein 1/3, envoplakin/periplakin antibodies), clinical exam for scarring of mucosa/ocular involvement, and age-appropriate malignancy screening to distinguish among these entities and guide therapy.
